question: What is the primary physical form of medication delivered by a nebulizer to the patient's lungs?

options.B: A fine mist or aerosolized vapor

explanation: A nebulizer turns liquid medicine into a vapor so the patient can easily breathe it deep into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is nebulization often chosen over other inhalers for patients in acute respiratory distress?

options.A: It requires only normal, quiet breathing instead of a deep, forced inhalation.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any vital sign monitoring.
options.C: It stops all lung infections within minutes of starting the treatment.
options.D: It works ten times faster than any intravenous medication available.

explanation: Patients struggling to catch their breath cannot coordinate deep inhalers, making normal breathing through a nebulizer mask much easier. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which medication group is most commonly given via nebulizer to relax tightened airway muscles?
explanation: Bronchodilators open up constricted breathing tubes so air can flow freely in and out of the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways and causing severe coughing. Which type of nebulized medication is most appropriate?
explanation: Mucolytics specifically target and break down thick pulmonary secretions, making them easier for the patient to expel. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason for assessing lung sounds before giving a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: To clear out thick mucus plugs before the machine is turned on
options.B: To establish a baseline for evaluating the treatment's effectiveness later
options.C: To find out if the patient has a hidden bacterial chest infection
options.D: To calculate the exact dose of medicine needed for the patient

explanation: Checking lung sounds beforehand helps the nurse compare wheezing or air entry after the treatment ends. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which physical sign indicates that a patient is experiencing severe respiratory distress before treatment?

options.A: A quiet, relaxed breathing pattern while lying flat
options.B: Pink skin color on the cheeks and nail beds
options.C: Use of accessory neck and chest muscles to breathe
options.D: A slow, even heart rate of 60 beats per minute

explanation: Straining neck and chest muscles means the body is working extra hard to pull air into struggling lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the usual gas flow rate range set on the flowmeter for a standard compressor nebulizer?
explanation: A flow rate of 6 to 8 liters per minute provides enough pressure to turn the liquid medicine into a proper mist. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is sterile normal saline sometimes added to the medication cup during preparation?

options.A: To reach the proper total liquid volume needed for the nebulizer cup to aerosolize correctly
options.B: To permanently neutralize any harmful side effects caused by bronchodilators
options.C: To numb the lining of the throat so the patient does not cough
options.D: To clean the plastic tubing before the medication mist passes through it

explanation: Nebulizer cups need a minimum fluid volume, often 3 to 5 mL, to create an effective aerosol mist. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h4)

question: What position should the nurse place the patient in before starting a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: Flat on their back with no pillows
options.C: Lying strictly on their left side

explanation: Sitting upright lets the chest expand fully, helping the medication travel deep into the lower airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why does the nurse occasionally tap the side of the medication cup during the procedure?

options.A: To prevent the plastic parts from overheating while the compressor runs
options.B: To help remaining liquid droplets slide down into the bottom of the cup to be aerosolized
options.C: To signal to the patient that the treatment session is halfway finished
options.D: To clear any dust blocking the outside air filter vents

explanation: Tapping the cup drops clinging fluid back into the reservoir so it doesn't go to waste on the walls. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take after the nebulizer cup runs dry?

options.A: Reassess lung sounds and measure the patient's oxygen saturation
options.B: Immediately start a second dose of medication without waiting
options.C: Disconnect the air flow meter and leave the room quietly
options.D: Instruct the patient to lie flat in bed for one hour

explanation: Checking lung sounds and oxygen levels right after treatment confirms whether the bronchodilator opened the airways successfully. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h6)

question: After a bronchodilator nebulizer treatment, a patient coughs heavily. What should the nurse encourage them to do next?

options.A: Swallow the mucus to keep the throat moist
options.B: Expectorate the loosened mucus into a tissue
options.C: Drink a large glass of ice-cold water immediately
options.D: Lie down flat on the bed to stop coughing

explanation: Coughing brings up the loosened secretions, so spitting them out into a tissue clears the airway safely. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which common side effect often occurs due to the stimulant properties of bronchodilators like albuterol?

options.D: Complete loss of the sense of taste

explanation: Beta-agonist bronchodilators stimulate heart receptors, frequently causing a fast heartbeat or jittery feeling. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: What should the nurse do FIRST if a patient suddenly develops severe wheezing and increased breathing distress right after starting a nebulizer?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the reaction goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the nebulizer treatment immediately and assess the patient
options.C: Ask the patient to lie flat and take deep, fast breaths
options.D: Turn up the air flow meter to make the mist spray faster

explanation: Worsening distress means a possible paradoxical bronchospasm, so stopping the drug is the immediate safety priority. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why is proper cleaning and drying of nebulizer equipment so critical for patient safety?

options.A: Dirty equipment will permanently break the air compressor motor
options.B: Washing prevents the plastic mask from changing color over time
options.C: Moist plastic parts easily grow harmful bacteria that can cause lung infections
options.D: Leftover medication residue turns into a solid metal inside the tube

explanation: Wet nebulizer cups are breeding grounds for germs, which the patient would inhale directly into their lungs during the next treatment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the correct way to dry nebulizer parts after washing them?

options.A: Air dry them completely on a clean paper towel or lint-free cloth
options.B: Blow hot air through them using a standard hair dryer on high heat
options.C: Place them inside a sealed plastic bag while they are still soaking wet
options.D: Wipe them dry using a heavily used cloth towel from the laundry bin

explanation: Air drying on a clean surface prevents germ transfer from dirty towels and ensures no moisture is trapped inside. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)
